clue.text: Step back and dance guys, the musicians are here!

indicators.note: stepping back means the word step is read from its end to its start

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned round
to hop is to dance or jig about
boys, as in 'the guys' meaning the lads

explanation.surface: A gig announcement: the band has arrived, so everybody stand aside and dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Step back' reads as an instruction to the crowd; it is the first piece, turned round. The Pet Shop Boys are an English synth-pop duo.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pet Shop Boys are a famous British pop duo, so they are a group of musicians.

clue.text: What to do with a 22 blunder

definitions.meaning: first meaning: 22 across is a Hush Puppy, a brand of shoe, and with a shoe you put your foot in it
second meaning: to make an embarrassing, tactless mistake

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to a shoe, so the literal reading is what you do with footwear; the idiom is the everyday sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to say or do something tactless, which is exactly a social blunder or gaffe.

clue.text: Letter from old reservists

wordplay.note: the Territorial Army with its article, abbreviated to two letters; Britain's volunteer force, since renamed the Army Reserve

explanation.surface: A letter received from former members of the army reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA was the Territorial Army, the UK's part-time volunteer reserve; 'old' because it is now called the Army Reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth character of the Greek alphabet, so it is a letter.

clue.text: Not all relationships terrify cool dude

indicators.note: only part of the letters of relationships terrify are used, the run that straddles the two words

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A laid-back guy who is scared of commitment, though not of every relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: A hipster is someone following the latest trendy fashions, a fashionably cool guy.

clue.text: Most elegant letters in The Lady? Just the opposite

indicators.note: the surface says the letters go inside the lady
reverses the 'in', so the lady goes inside the letters instead

parts.note: post, the mail that arrives
she, the pronoun for a lady

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the smartest correspondence appears in The Lady, a genteel British magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lady is a long-running British magazine for gentlewomen, which suits the posh surface; 'Just the opposite' flips which piece goes inside which.
explanation.definitionFit: Posh means smart and upper-class, so the superlative is the most stylish or elegant.

clue.text: Barely downplay every other sauce on taco starter

indicators.note: only the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of downplay are kept

parts.note: the word read for its even letters
jus, thin gravy made from meat juices

indicators.note: the opening letter of taco

parts.note: the word whose opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Playing down a dressing that is spooned onto the first taco.
explanation.definitionFit: Only just and barely both describe something achieved by the narrowest of margins.

clue.text: Stay focused two seconds before one gets into fancy photo tent

parts.note: two words for a second: S, its abbreviation, and tick, as in 'just a tick'

indicators.note: the letter for one is placed inside the rearranged letters
in its sense of elaborate or fanciful, the letters are dressed up into a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder
I, the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A photographer's instructions: hold still briefly while someone climbs into an elaborate tent used for product photography.
explanation.walkthrough: A tick is British informal for a moment, as in 'just a tick'; with S for second it gives two seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick to the point is to keep to the relevant subject without digressing, so to stay focused.

clue.text: Stubborn diner on diet starts to eat egg over easy

indicators.note: the first letters take in the next piece as if eating it
the opening letters of diner, on and diet

parts.note: the three words whose first letters are taken

indicators.note: an egg cooked over easy is flipped over, so the word egg is turned round

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned

explanation.surface: A determined diner on a diet who still tucks into eggs fried over easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over easy' is an American term for an egg fried on both sides, which here signals flipping the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogged describes someone who persists tenaciously, which is a stubborn determination.

clue.text: Science chief listens for marine creatures

indicators.note: the head, so the first letter of science

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken
harks, an old word for pays attention to sounds

explanation.surface: The head of science pays attention to sea creatures, perhaps hearing whale song.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharks are predatory fish that live in the sea, so they are ocean animals.

clue.text: Rising damp finally puts an end to hut one rebuilt

indicators.note: the last piece is placed at the end of what came before
the letters of hut one are put back together in a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder

indicators.note: the closing letter of damp

parts.note: the word whose last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A hut is rebuilt because rising damp got into its walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising damp' reads as a building fault, but rising is the definition and damp only gives its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: On the up is an idiom for improving or increasing, so it means rising or climbing.

clue.text: They say what the chippy does is not altruistic

indicators.note: what people say, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: a chippy is a British fish and chip shop, and it sells fish

explanation.surface: Remarks that the local chippy is unkind to its customers.
explanation.walkthrough: A chippy here is a British fish and chip shop, not a carpenter, which is the other everyday British meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone selfish puts their own interests first, the opposite of an altruistic, generous person.

clue.text: Gauntlet thrown about before beginning a shoot-out

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the next piece
the letters of gauntlet are thrown into disorder and rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder

indicators.note: the first letter of before

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A challenge is issued, the gauntlet thrown down, before a duel begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gauntlet thrown' suggests throwing down a challenge, which fits the duel; here it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun battle is a fight with firearms, an exchange of shots like a shoot-out.

clue.text: Jeer half-heartedly about fine comedian

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the next piece
one of the two letters at the heart of jeer is dropped, halving its middle

parts.note: the word that loses a middle letter
OK, as in 'that's fine'

explanation.surface: Heckling a standup comic without much conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: A joker is someone who tells jokes or clowns around, so a comic or comedian.

clue.text: Pinch and run

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to hurry or sprint

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinch and run' reads like a thief's instructions to steal and flee; the words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a tiny measure added in cooking and a quick sprint.

clue.text: Activists disrupting top resorts

indicators.note: the letters of top resorts are thrown into disorder and rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, used letter for letter

explanation.surface: Demonstrators causing trouble at the most popular holiday destinations.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual spelling ends -ers, but -ors is a recognised variant.
explanation.definitionFit: Protestors campaign publicly against something, as political activists or demonstrators do.

clue.text: Me? I'm not sure to follow twist about politician

definitions.note: the setter speaking, the person who made this crossword

indicators.note: the hesitant sound comes after the rest
the twisted piece goes around the politician

parts.note: coil, to wind or twist round
MP, Member of Parliament
er, the noise of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone unsure of themselves following a politician's twisting statements.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'me' or 'I' can mean the setter, here the person who put the puzzle together.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter of a crossword is its compiler, the person who made the grid and clues.

clue.text: One overeating confectionery gets belly ache drinking dodgy hooch

indicators.note: the stomach pain takes in the next piece as if swallowing it

parts.note: colic, abdominal pain

indicators.note: dubious or unreliable, so the letters of hooch are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone who binges on sweets ends up with a stomach ache after drinking bad moonshine.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocoholic is a person addicted to chocolate, who eats far too much of that sweet treat.

clue.text: Tea before 5 on vacation, very defnitely not 4

definitions.note: 4 down is posh at its most elegant; this is the opposite

parts.note: cha, a British slang word for tea
V, the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: vacated, so the middle letters of very leave and only its ends stay

parts.note: the word emptied of its middle, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Tea taken before five while on holiday is very much not the poshest thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Chav is British slang, often snobbish, for a loutish young person; 4 down points to its opposite. The misspelling 'defnitely' is the printed clue's.
explanation.definitionFit: Chavvy describes a brash, lowbrow style, the reverse of something smart and upper-class.

clue.text: Cook the old man clam after shelling? Mon Dieu!

indicators.note: each word has its outside letters taken off, like shelling a clam, leaving only the insides

parts.note: shelled to its two middle letters
shelled to its middle letter
shelled to its middle letter
shelled to its middle letter
shelled to its two middle letters

explanation.surface: Someone asked to cook the old man a clam, without its shell, reacts in mock French dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like an instruction to rearrange, but it is one of the words shelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are French exclamations of surprise, used in English for something startling or risque.

clue.text: Where some apples end up, said one who knows

indicators.note: spoken aloud, so the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: in cider, since apples are pressed to make cider

explanation.surface: Someone well informed explains where certain apples finish up.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider is someone within an organisation with privileged knowledge, so a person in the know.

clue.text: Jezebel's man got it? Bravo!

parts.note: aha, the exclamation when something becomes clear
B in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone guesses Jezebel's husband and is cheered for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Bravo reads as applause, but it is the radio code word for B. In the Bible Jezebel was married to Ahab, king of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: King Ahab was Jezebel's husband in the Old Testament book of Kings.

clue.text: Youthful one entering club to play tennis match at last

indicators.note: the numeral goes into the string of final letters
the last letter of each of club, to, play, tennis and match

parts.note: the five words whose last letters are taken
I, the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A young player joins a club to take part in a tennis match at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Boyish means like a young boy in looks or manner, so youthful and fresh-faced.

clue.text: Misbehave with current male

parts.note: AC, alternating current
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: Behaving badly alongside an ordinary present-day man.
explanation.walkthrough: A tup is the British dialect word for a ram, a male sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to behave badly, as children or faulty machines do, so to misbehave.

clue.text: Quiet pet, one of a pair?

parts.note: hush, silence
a puppy, a young dog kept as a pet

explanation.surface: A silent dog that is one of a matching pair.
explanation.walkthrough: Hush Puppies are a brand of casual suede shoe, which come in pairs; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hush Puppy is a shoe brand, and any shoe is one of a pair worn together.

clue.text: Double alcohol percentage for validation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in the US the ... rating of a spirit is twice its alcohol by volume
second meaning: evidence that establishes something is true

explanation.walkthrough: In the American system a 40 per cent spirit is 80 proof, so proof is double the alcohol percentage.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof is both a measure of spirit strength and evidence that confirms or verifies a claim.

clue.text: Standard American banks invested in house

indicators.note: money invested in property is put into it, so the short piece is placed inside the house

parts.note: villa, a large detached house

indicators.note: the outer edges of American, like the two banks of a river

parts.note: the word reduced to its outer letters

explanation.surface: US banks have put their money into property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American banks' reads as financial institutions; banks here are the outer letters of American.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla in the informal sense means plain or ordinary, the basic standard version of something.

clue.text: Casual get-togethers of medical practitioner circle before cutback

parts.note: Dr, doctor
O, the shape of a circle
snip, a cut, written back to front

explanation.surface: Informal gatherings for doctors' groups ahead of spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutback' looks like a reduction in spending, but it splits into cut, a snip, and back, which turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Drop-ins are informal sessions or visits that people may attend without an appointment, casual gatherings.

clue.text: How to reach for a tip and make money

definitions.text: How to reach for a tip
definitions.meaning: first meaning: rearranging the letters of 'for a tip' turns them into 'a profit'
second meaning: to earn more than you spend

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a reverse anagram: you get from 'for a tip' to the answer's last two words by turning, that is rearranging, its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that turns a profit earns more than it spends, so it is making money.
